In our international public law there are a few contradictory principles, and if you observe our court system when it comes to trials for illegal immigrants, you can see this. First is the "Territory Principal" where crimes committed in a territory would be subject to the law of the territory. Hence why the USA can still put illegal immigrants in jail. However international law also holds he "Nationality Principal", where the government of a citizen can obtain jurisdiction over its citizens when that citizen is abroad. That's also how the Mexican government brings cartel members in the USA back to Mexico, and how the US government back US citizens that commit crimes overseas. For more info:

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_jurisdiction_over_international_defendants_in_the_United_States
